test.title: Mirror Exam 2 — the same seven question types, new numbers (matches the Mirror Exam PDF)
test.intro: Work each part on paper exactly as you would on the exam, type your final answer, then press Check answer. Probabilities to 4 decimals; means and SDs to 2. Start the 50-minute timer first if you want the real feel.

questions.prompt:
Commuting and Housing. The table below summarizes how 110 students at a university commute and where they live.
Commute | Lives on campus | Lives off campus
Drive | 8 | 34
Bus | 10 | 16
Walk | 22 | 4
Bike | 9 | 7
Total on campus = 49, Total off campus = 61, Overall Total = 110.

parts.label: (a) 1 pt
parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected student lives off campus?
parts.solution:
one category → its total ÷ grand total
P(off campus) = 61/110 = 0.5545

parts.label: (b) 1 pt
parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected student walks to campus?

parts.label: (c) 1 pt
parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected student drives OR lives on campus?
parts.solution:
OR → add, then subtract the overlap (drive AND on campus = 8) once
P(drive or on) = 42/110 + 49/110 − 8/110 = 83/110 = 0.7545
Forgetting the overlap gives 91/110 = 0.8273 ✗

parts.label: (d) 1 pt
parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected student bikes AND lives off campus?
parts.solution:
AND → the one cell ÷ 110
P(bike and off) = 7/110 = 0.0636

parts.label: (e) 2 pt
parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected student takes the bus given that the student lives off campus?
parts.solution:
GIVEN off campus → divide by the off-campus total (61), not 110
P(bus | off) = 16/61 = 0.2623
16/110 = 0.1455 is the classic wrong denominator ✗

questions.prompt:
Discrete Probability Distribution. Determine whether the following distribution represents a valid discrete probability distribution. If not, explain why.
x | P(x)
1 | 0.15
2 | 0.25
3 | 0.30
4 | 0.20
5 | 0.12

parts.label: (i)
parts.question: Add the probabilities. What do they sum to?

parts.label: (ii)
parts.question: Valid or not valid?
parts.answer: NOT valid — each P(x) is between 0 and 1, but the probabilities add to 1.02, not 1.
parts.solution:
Rule 1: every P(x) is between 0 and 1 ✓
Rule 2: Σ P(x) = 1.02 ≠ 1 ✗
Not a valid probability distribution (write both checks — the question says explain why).

questions.prompt:
Cars per Household. A city planner records the number of cars, X, owned by each household in a random sample of 85 households. No household owned more than 3 cars.
x | Frequency
0 | 13
1 | 29
2 | 33
3 | 10

parts.label: (a) 2 pt
parts.question: Construct a probability distribution for X (give P(0), P(1), P(2), P(3) to 4 decimals).

parts.label: (b) 2 pt
parts.question: Graph the discrete probability distribution (describe it in words).
parts.answer: x across (0, 1, 2, 3), P(x) up; a vertical bar above each x with heights 0.1529, 0.3412, 0.3882, 0.1176; tallest at x = 2; label both axes.
parts.solution:
Horizontal axis: x = 0, 1, 2, 3. Vertical axis: P(x), 0 to about 0.4.
A vertical bar (or line) above each x with height equal to its probability; the tallest is at x = 2.
Label both axes — part of the credit.

parts.label: (c) 2 pt
parts.question: Compute the mean of X (2 decimals). Then write the interpretation sentence on paper.
parts.solution:
μ = Σ x·P(x) = 0(0.1529) + 1(0.3412) + 2(0.3882) + 3(0.1176)
= 0 + 0.3412 + 0.7764 + 0.3528 = 1.4704 ≈ 1.47 cars
Interpretation: over many households in this neighborhood, the average number of cars per household is about 1.47.

parts.label: (d) 2 pt
parts.question: Compute the standard deviation of X (2 decimals).

questions.prompt: Reading Habits. According to a national survey, 35% of U.S. adults read at least one book last month. In a random sample of 8 U.S. adults, find the probability that:

parts.label: (a) 2 pt
parts.question: Exactly 2 read at least one book last month.

parts.label: (b) 2 pt
parts.question: At most 2 read at least one book last month.
parts.answer: 0.4278 (0.4279 if you add the rounded terms — both accepted)

parts.label: (c) 2 pt
parts.question: At least 1 read at least one book last month.

parts.label: (d) 2 pt
parts.question: For a random sample of 300 U.S. adults, find the expected number and the standard deviation of those who read at least one book last month.

questions.prompt: Shuttle Wait Time. Suppose the waiting time X (in minutes) for a campus shuttle is uniformly distributed between 0 and 25 minutes.

parts.label: (a) 1 pt
parts.question: Sketch or describe the graph of the uniform pdf. Type the height of the rectangle (4 decimals).
parts.answer: height = 1/25 = 0.0400; a flat line (rectangle) from 0 to 25, 0 elsewhere; area = 1
parts.solution:
height = 1/(b − a) = 1/(25 − 0) = 1/25 = 0.04
A flat line at 0.04 from x = 0 to x = 25 (and 0 outside); area = 25 × 0.04 = 1 ✓

parts.label: (b) 2 pt
parts.question: Find P(5 ≤ X ≤ 15).

parts.label: (c) 2 pt
parts.question: Find P(X > 18).

questions.prompt: Normal Distribution and z-Scores. Hints (as printed on the exam): P(Z < −0.85) = 0.1977, P(Z < −1.30) = 0.0968, P(Z < −0.25) = 0.4013, P(Z < 1.25) = 0.8944.

parts.label: (a) 2 pt
parts.question: Find the area to the left of z = −0.85.
parts.solution: Area to the LEFT of a negative z: the hint P(Z < −0.85) = 0.1977 is already the answer (no 1 − needed).

parts.label: (b) 2 pt
parts.question: Find the area between z = −1.30 and z = −0.25.
parts.solution:
between = (left of the bigger z) − (left of the smaller z); −0.25 is bigger than −1.30
0.4013 − 0.0968 = 0.3045

parts.label: (c) 2 pt
parts.question: X is normally distributed with μ = 250 and σ = 40. Find P(X > 300).

questions.prompt: Heights of Adult Men. Heights of adult men in the U.S. are approximately normally distributed with mean μ = 69 inches and standard deviation σ = 2.8 inches. Hints (as printed on the exam): P(Z < 1.79) = 0.9633, P(Z < −1.43) = 0.0764, P(Z < −1.07) = 0.1423, P(Z < 1.07) = 0.8577; the 10th percentile corresponds to z = −1.28.

parts.label: (a) 2 pt
parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected man is taller than 74 inches?

parts.label: (b) 2 pt
parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected man is shorter than 65 inches?
parts.solution:
z = (65 − 69)/2.8 = −1.43
P(X < 65) = left of −1.43 = 0.0764 (the hint is already the left area)

parts.label: (c) 2 pt
parts.question: What proportion of men are between 66 and 72 inches tall?

parts.label: (d) 2 pt
parts.question: What height places a man at the 10th percentile? (1 decimal)
parts.solution:
10th percentile → area to the LEFT = 0.10 → hint z = −1.28 (negative: lower tail)
x = μ + zσ = 69 + (−1.28)(2.8) = 69 − 3.584 = 65.416 ≈ 65.4 inches
